note: Iowa runs a separate number for abuse suspected inside a licensed facility or program, distinct from the general child abuse hotline - use it if what happened was inside a program. Iowa also folded its Board of Psychology into the Board of Behavioral Health Professionals in 2024, so one board now covers psychologists along with counselors and social workers. And the Iowa Office of Ombudsman covers both the licensing boards and Health and Human Services, which makes it the escalation route when either one stalls.

civil_injury.summary: Two years from the injury for any personal injury claim, including assault, battery, false imprisonment and negligence.
civil_injury.quote: 2. Injuries to person or reputation - relative rights - statute penalty. Those founded on injuries to the person or reputation, including injuries to relative rights, whether based on contract or tort, or for a statute penalty, within two years.
civil_injury.note: One period for intentional torts and negligence. 2026 Iowa Acts, SF 512 (effective July 1, 2026) adds that nothing in § 614.1 alters the law on when a claim accrues, 'including the discovery rule' (per the Legislative Services Agency 2026 Summary of Legislation, https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/publications/SOL/1611625.pdf); the bill text itself was not read.

civil_minor_tolling.summary: Yes. As of July 1, 2026, someone injured as a child has until five years after turning 18 (age 23) to sue. Before that change the extension was only one year after turning 18. It also applies to claims against the state and local governments.
civil_minor_tolling.citation: Iowa Code § 614.8(2), as amended by 2026 Iowa Acts, HF 1036, § 5 (effective July 1, 2026)
civil_minor_tolling.quote: the times limited for actions in this chapter, or chapter 216, 659A, 669, or 670, except those brought for penalties and forfeitures, are extended in favor of minors, so that they shall have one year five years from and after attainment of majority
civil_minor_tolling.note: The quote is from the enrolled bill, where 'one year' is struck and 'five years' inserted (strike-through formatting is lost in text extraction; the LSA 2026 summary table lists § 614.8(2) as amended by HF 1036 § 5, signed May 15, 2026, effective July 1, 2026). The Iowa Code 2026 compilation on the code site (https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/614.8.pdf) still reads 'one year' because it predates the Act. The Act does not say whether it revives claims already expired under the one-year rule. No general discovery rule for non-sexual abuse; § 614.8A covers sexual abuse and human trafficking only.

civil_government_claims.summary: Against the State of Iowa, a written claim must be filed with the Department of Management within two years; the State cannot be sued for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Against a city, county or school district, the lawsuit must be filed within two years of the injury. Minors get the extension described above in both cases.
civil_government_claims.quote: Except as provided in section 614.8, a claim or suit otherwise permitted under this chapter shall be forever barred, unless within two years after the claim accrued, the claim is made in writing and filed with the director of the department of management
civil_government_claims.note: § 669.14(4) excludes 'Any claim arising out of assault, battery, false imprisonment'. § 670.5 (municipalities, https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/670.5.pdf): 'shall commence an action therefor within two years after the alleged wrongful death, loss, or injury', with no separate notice requirement.

criminal_child_abuse.summary: Felony child endangerment against a child under 18 (causing bodily injury, serious injury or death) can be charged at any time; there is no deadline. Misdemeanor child endangerment must be charged within 3 years.
criminal_child_abuse.quote: An information or indictment for the following offenses committed on or with a person who is under the age of eighteen years may be commenced at any time after the commission of the offense: ... 6. Child endangerment in violation of section 726.6, subsection 5, 6, or 7.
criminal_child_abuse.note: Before July 1, 2026: § 726.6(5) (death, class B), (6) (serious injury, class C), (7) (bodily injury, class D). Child endangerment covers a 'person having custody or control over a child', which § 726.6(4) defines to include a person who 'has accepted, undertaken, or assumed supervision of a child ... from the parent or guardian', which fits program staff. Aggravated-misdemeanor child endangerment (§ 726.6(8)) falls under § 802.3's 3 years. 2026 Iowa Acts HF 2360 (effective July 1, 2026; enrolled text https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/publications/LGE/91/HF2360.pdf) added a definition as new subsection 1 and renumbered the penalty subsections: death is now (6), serious injury (7), bodily injury (8). HF 2360 did not amend § 802.2B, which still cites 'subsection 5, 6, or 7'. The Iowa Code editor normally updates such internal references, but until the 2027 Code is published, confirm that bodily-injury child endangerment (now (8)) is still covered by the no-limit rule. § 802.2B last amended 2021 Iowa Acts ch. 102.

criminal_felony_assault.summary: Felony assault (for example, assault causing serious injury) must be charged within 3 years. Iowa uses the same 3 years for aggravated and serious misdemeanor assault; simple misdemeanor assault must be charged within 1 year.
criminal_felony_assault.quote: In all cases, except those enumerated in section 802.1, 802.2, 802.2A, 802.2B, 802.2C, 802.2D, 802.2E, 802.2F, 802.2G, or 802.10, an indictment or information for a felony or aggravated or serious misdemeanor shall be found within three years after its commission.
criminal_felony_assault.note: § 708.2(5): assault causing serious injury is a class D felony; (1) and (3) aggravated misdemeanors; (2) serious misdemeanor; (7) simple misdemeanor. § 802.4: simple misdemeanor 'within one year'. § 802.6: time out of state is excluded. 2026 Iowa Acts SF 2218 amended § 802.3 only to add a new § 802.2H (election misconduct).

channels.name: Iowa Board of Behavioral Health Professionals
channels.what_it_can_do: Receives and investigates complaints against mental health counselors, marriage and family therapists, social workers, behavior analysts and - since the boards merged under 2024 Iowa Acts SF 2385 - psychologists, and disciplines their licences. Iowa publishes its discipline documents.
channels.who_to_report: Any licensed behavioral health professional in Iowa. Anyone may file: a patient, a family member, anyone else.
channels.how: File through the Department of Inspections, Appeals and Licensing complaints page, which routes it to the right board.
channels.note: Iowa law keeps the complainant's information confidential.

channels.name: Iowa reporting of abuse in a licensed facility
channels.what_it_can_do: The route Iowa gives for abuse suspected inside a licensed facility or program, separate from the general child abuse hotline.
channels.who_to_report: A young person abused inside an Iowa licensed facility or program.
channels.how: Call the facility line rather than the general hotline.
channels.phone_note: For abuse suspected in a licensed facility or program.

channels.name: Iowa Child Abuse Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide confidential 24-hour line taking reports of suspected abuse of children and dependent adults. The Child Protective Services intake unit screens them.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Iowa program.
channels.how: Call. Have identifying details and the child's whereabouts ready.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
channels.note: You may stay anonymous unless you are reporting as a mandatory reporter, in which case you have to leave your name and contact details.

channels.name: Iowa Office of Ombudsman
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office that reviews complaints about state agencies, and it names both the professional licensing boards and the Department of Health and Human Services among the bodies it covers. The route when a licensing complaint or an abuse report has gone nowhere.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It examines how an agency handled something rather than disciplining a clinician or a program itself.
channels.who_to_report: Somebody who has already complained to an Iowa board or to HHS and got no response they can make sense of.

channels.name: Disability Rights Iowa
channels.what_it_can_do: Iowa's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Iowa program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.

channels.name: Iowa HHS facility licensing and certification
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and certifies Iowa's residential facilities and programs for children, and takes the complaints about abuse inside them through its dedicated facility reporting line.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Iowa facility or program.
channels.how: Use the facility abuse line for abuse inside a licensed program, and the Department's contacts page for anything else.
channels.phone_note: For abuse suspected in a licensed facility or program.
